Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Nepal's reply as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The UAE fielders have taken their respective fielding positions as Arjun Saud and Kushal Bhurtel stride out to open the inning for Nepal. Junaid Siddique has the new ball in his hand and will begin proceedings. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Nepal bat deep and will fancy themselves to chase 182 in their allotted overs. UAE will hope to exploit the new ball and get some early wickets to put pressure on their opponents. Can the United Arab Emirates defend this and make a match of this despite their disappointing batting effort? Or will Nepal trot home to an easy win? We shall find out shortly when we return for the run chase.

Sandeep Lamichhane is up for a chat. He says that after a long time in the tournament, he has managed to find his rhythm and he bowled well in this game. Claims that the wicket suited the spinners and he tried to bowl in the right areas. Mentions that he took three balls to set up Rameez Shahzad’s wicket as first was a leg break, then the googly, and finally bowled a flipper which got him stuck in the crease. Reckons that they bat deep so this should be an easy chase but they need to go and bat deep. Adds that if they play all their overs they will get to target with ease.

Mustafa’s dismissal led to a flurry of wickets as the lower order of UAE crumbled under pressure and could not add much. They were dismissed in the 47th over for just 181. Sandeep Lamichhane was the pick of the Nepalese bowlers with terrific figures of 3 for 23 in his 10-over spell. Karan KC was impressive as well snapping 3 for 36. The likes of Pratish GC, Dipendra Singh Airee, and Gulsan Jha took one apiece to complete an all-around effort by the Nepalese bowlers. They have done the job and it is now on the batters to get them over the finish line.

An outstanding effort with the ball by Nepal allows them to restrict UAE to a below-par score of 181. Having put into bat first, UAE got off to a poor start losing Asif Khan for a second ball duck. Aryansh Sharma and Vriitya Aravind steadied the innings with a 64-run stand. The wicket of Sharma put the brakes on scoring for UAE and the batters found it difficult to tackle the Nepal attack. Nepal soon picked up Rameez Shahzad and Aravind in quick succession and had them reeling at 97 for 4 in the 28th over. Rohan Mustafa and Basil Hameed got together and stitched another 58 runs for the 5th wicket. Both the batters were dismissed after getting handy starts.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the prematch formalities and the game is set to begin as the umpires walk towards the pitch. The Nepal players are in a huddle at the boundary line before taking their respective positions on the field. Asif Khan and Aryansh Sharma will open the inning for UAE and will want to get a good partnership going here. Karan KC has the new ball in his hand and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's play...

We are set for the game to start but first the two sets of players and the umpires lineup for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of the United Arab Emirates first followed by Nepal's national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is out in the center for the pitch report. He mentions that it is quite chilly at the moment but will warm up as the day progresses. Says that there is a breeze blowing from east to west and the pitch is bang center so the captains would not find it difficult to decide which side to bowl the spinner or the seamers. Claims that it is a place to chase as four of the six games have been won by the team batting second. Adds that this surface was used three matches ago. Shares that there is a bit of grass on the surface which should help the bowlers get some swing early. Ends by saying that the batters need to keep their discipline and will be able to set a good target.

Vriitya Aravind the captain of United Arab Emirates says it’s a great privilege to lead the country. Adds that he is the 11th player to lead UAE. Says that they were looking to bowl first too as the first 15 overs will give help to the pacers. Mentions that they have 3 changes as well.

Rohit Paudel the skipper of Nepal says looking at conditions they would prefer to bowl first. Claims that they needed to correct a few things so the gap is good for them. Informs that they have three changes and some of them are due to injuries.

TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favor of Nepal. They have elected to BOWL first.

UAE, on the other hand, had a horrific outing in the group stage. They failed to win a single encounter and ended at the bottom of the table in Group B. Their batting did not turn up in this tournament and they lost by huge margins against their opponents. UAE skipper Muhammad Waseem and the experienced Rohan Mustafa will have to share the bulk of responsibility while youngsters like Ali Naseer, Aayan Khan, and Vriitya Aravind have been impressive and will hope to be the torchbearers of UAE cricket going forward. Nepal have had the better of UAE in recent times and UAE will surely want to settle the scores today. An exciting contest is up on our hands. Stay tuned as we bring you the toss and team news in a short while.

Nepal had a solitary win in the group stage against the USA and finished fourth in the table with just 2 points. Their batters did a decent job but the bowlers failed to contain or pick wickets at crucial intervals. The likes of Kushal Bhurtel, Aasif Sheikh, and Bhim Sharki were impressive with the bat while Karan KC did a fine job with the ball.  Nepal will look to put a fine effort against the fellow Asian side and continue their progress on the world stage.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 7th place playoff semi-final number two between Nepal and UAE to be played at the Takashinga Sports Club in Harare. The winner of this game will face Ireland in the 7th place play-off final. The World Cup qualifiers did not go as per plan and both these teams are playing for pride in this contest.
